source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use the same CDC example sequence for all PPE ensembles and locations because sequence consistency is the main protection against self-contamination.","B":"Use the approved doffing sequence, avoid contaminating skin or clothing, discard PPE appropriately, and perform hand hygiene.","C":"Touch the front of the gown freely once gloves are removed because it is then considered clean.","D":"Wear contaminated gown and gloves to the nurses’ station and remove them after documentation."}}
source_row.rationale: The safety goal during doffing is to prevent self-contamination. CDC provides example sequences, but the exact order can vary with the PPE ensemble and isolation workflow. Staff should use the approved sequence, avoid touching contaminated PPE surfaces to skin or clothing, dispose of PPE appropriately, and perform hand hygiene.
source_row.source_detail: CDC Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices — PPE removal/hand hygiene: remove and discard PPE to avoid contaminating skin/clothing and perform hand hygiene; sequence depends on ensemble/workflow. source_row.stem: A nurse is removing contaminated gown and gloves after patient care. Which principle is most important when doffing PPE?
